chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'The heart becomes such that there is in it neither faith nor disbelief, resembling a lump of meat. Has not any one of you found that?'

key_terms.مُضْغَة: Lump of meat (metaphor for an intermediate, indistinct state)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual state of a heart that is neither fully faithful nor disbelieving?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the metaphor of a 'lump of meat' (مُضْغَة) to describe a spiritual state of stagnation where the heart possesses faith but lacks the vitality of conviction, remaining neither fully alive nor dead. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, serves as a diagnostic tool for self-reflection, urging believers to identify this intermediate condition and actively cultivate the dynamic qualities of faith to avoid spiritual paralysis. The imagery highlights the Shia emphasis on the heart's capacity for both spiritual growth and decay, linking internal state to external religious practice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Abbas Bin Marouf, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’farasws saying: ‘الْقَلْبُ’ The heart (sometimes) becomes such that there is neither Emān in it nor Kufr (disbelief), resembling a lump. Hasn’t any one of you found that?’
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al- ‘Abbas ibn Ma’ruf from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar from abu Basir who has said the following:
“I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘There is the heart in which there is no belief or disbelief, like a chunk of flesh. Does any one of you feel it is as such sometimes?’”
